result.summary: The intersection features marked zebra crosswalks and continuous sidewalks within a residential setting. Safety is limited by significant visual obstructions from a large tree and parked cars near the crossing, as well as the absence of visible pedestrian-specific signals.

hazards.name: Visual Obstruction from Vegetation
hazards.description: A large, dense tree on the corner significantly blocks the sightline between drivers and pedestrians waiting to cross.
hazards.location_in_image: Right side of the image, at the corner near the traffic light.

hazards.name: Lack of Daylighting
hazards.description: Parked vehicles are located close to the intersection, reducing visibility of pedestrians entering the crosswalk.
hazards.location_in_image: Along the curbs on both sides of the street approaching the intersection.

interventions.title: Daylighting and Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Install curb extensions to shorten crossing distance and prevent parking near the crosswalk, improving visibility.

interventions.title: Pedestrian Signal Installation
interventions.description: Install dedicated pedestrian countdown signals to provide clear right-of-way information.

interventions.title: Vegetation Management
interventions.description: Prune or replace the large tree at the corner to ensure clear sightlines and visibility of the traffic signal.

result.summary: The residential environment provides a sidewalk but lacks formal crossing infrastructure such as marked crosswalks or curb ramps. A pedestrian is visible in the roadway, highlighting the risk posed by the absence of designated, protected crossing points and sightline obstructions from parked cars.

hazards.name: Unmarked Crossing
hazards.description: Pedestrians are crossing at an intersection or mid-block point with no marked crosswalk to alert drivers.
hazards.location_in_image: Center foreground where the pedestrian is walking

hazards.name: Sightline Obstruction
hazards.description: Parked vehicles along the curb block the visibility between drivers and pedestrians entering the roadway.
hazards.location_in_image: Right side of the street along the curb

hazards.name: Lack of Curb Ramps
hazards.description: No visible ADA-compliant ramps to facilitate safe transition from the sidewalk to the street level.
hazards.location_in_image: Corner of the sidewalk on the left

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalk
interventions.description: Install continental-style marked crosswalks to clearly define pedestrian right-of-way.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions (Bulb-outs)
interventions.description: Extend the sidewalk into the parking lane to shorten crossing distance and improve visibility.

interventions.title: Intersection Daylighting
interventions.description: Remove parking spaces closest to the intersection to ensure clear sightlines for all road users.

result.summary: The image shows a wide, uncontrolled pedestrian crossing with high-visibility markings across a multi-lane roadway. While a crosswalk is present, the lack of continuous paved sidewalks and the long crossing distance across four lanes of traffic create a high-exposure environment for pedestrians.

hazards.name: Long Crossing Distance
hazards.description: The wide, four-lane roadway requires pedestrians to be exposed to traffic for an extended period without a refuge island.

hazards.name: Discontinuous Sidewalks
hazards.description: The lack of paved, continuous sidewalks forces pedestrians to walk on unpaved shoulders or in the roadway to reach the crossing.
hazards.location_in_image: Left and right sides of the roadway

interventions.title: Pedestrian Refuge Island
interventions.description: Install a raised island in the center of the crosswalk to allow pedestrians to cross one direction of traffic at a time.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Extend the sidewalk into the roadway at the crossing to shorten the crossing distance and improve visibility between drivers and pedestrians.

interventions.title: Sidewalk Paving and Extension
interventions.description: Construct continuous, ADA-compliant paved sidewalks on both sides of the street to provide a safe, separated path.

result.summary: The intersection features high-visibility continental crosswalks and continuous sidewalks, serving a mixed-use residential and commercial area. While basic infrastructure like curb ramps and traffic signals are present, the wide crossing distance and lack of dedicated pedestrian signals increase exposure risk for people crossing.

hazards.name: Long crossing distance
hazards.description: The width of the roadway increases the time pedestrians are exposed to traffic without a refuge island.
hazards.location_in_image: Across the main roadway at the marked crosswalks.

hazards.name: Lack of visible pedestrian signals
hazards.description: No dedicated pedestrian signal heads are visible, forcing pedestrians to rely on vehicular signals which may not account for walking speeds or turning conflicts.
hazards.location_in_image: At the corners of the intersection near the traffic light poles.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions (Bulb-outs)
interventions.description: Extend the sidewalk into the parking lane to shorten crossing distance and improve visibility between drivers and pedestrians.

interventions.title: Pedestrian Countdown Signals
interventions.description: Install dedicated pedestrian signals with countdown timers to provide clear information on remaining crossing time.

interventions.title: Leading Pedestrian Interval (LPI)
interventions.description: Program the traffic signal to give pedestrians a 3-7 second head start before the parallel vehicle green light.
